q: This would be my second pregnancy. First one 10 years ago. So I feel like I'm relearning everything.
cx: Six weeks, planned second pregnancy ten years after a surprise first.

q: My son was a surprise, so to be planning this, and older, working in health care, I'm much more scared than I was when I was 20.
cx: Second pregnancy after ten years.

q: I think everything being out on social media definitely increases the fear. It can be helpful, but when I was young and naive, i didn't worry about as much lol.
cx: Comparing this pregnancy with her first, ten years ago.

q: Classes are in cohorts so I can’t just take less classes or try to do the degree slower. I can’t take a gap year (not allowed) it’s a one and done type of situation.
cx: 12 weeks, first-year pharmacy student working 16 hours a week, due in November.

q: I don’t even really get a full 6 weeks off since I’ll have to finish school out online.
cx: Due mid-semester.

q: Cried at the hospital bathroom after they told me I can’t do CTG without eating anything even though what they said was reasonable, but I’m at that level of being emotionally and physically exhausted.
cx: At 37 weeks, first visit at the hospital where she will give birth.

q: I feel like I need the longest hug in the world, and I don’t want it to end until baby is here. Everything hurts 😭.
cx: Venting at 37 weeks.

q: Since this is my second I’m really hoping I’ll go into spontaneous labor.
cx: After an induced first birth where the epidural did not work for hours.

q: I’m very scared for both and I don’t know what to do. I know I won’t feel pain but the whole staying in hospital for days, having to push or worse, being cut OPEN.
cx: At 27+5, a planned induction with a caesarean as back-up.

q: How quickly do they really grow out because I don’t want to over buy and be left with so many 0-3 months clothes or 3-6 month clothes just for her to outgrow it so quickly.
cx: First-time mother due in August, nesting.

q: My husband works nights so I’m also trying to avoid doing laundry everyday if I can help it.
cx: Why she wants enough newborn clothes.

q: unfortunately my whole family lives in CA and I’m currently in VA. I’ve shared my registry but I don’t really have a ton of close friends and my family hasn’t sent anything so I’ve only been given a few things from our registry :/
cx: Asked whether she would have a shower.

q: At my job I’m usually outside for the entire or at least majority of my shift. I also live in a particularly hot state, so in the next few weeks I know it’s going to get rough being outside.
cx: 19 years old, 24 weeks, garden-centre worker lifting pallets and soil.

q: I am a bit embarrassed about telling work as I am young, and because my job is also not made for a pregnant person.
cx: Has not told work or asked her OB about restrictions.

q: I also don’t know how to go about asking for restrictions from my ob, I don’t have another appointment for a month, so I guess I would have to call the office(?)
cx: Asking how to get work restrictions.

q: I hate being seen differently or as less helpful.
cx: Why she hasn't asked her employer for changes.

q: I work as a joiner so I’m on my feet all day in heavy steel caps. I’m so sore and tired at the end of each day
cx: First-time mother at 29+3, back at work after four months off sick.

q: I feel silly even thinking about starting leave early because I still have a ways to go and so many women work all the way up until they deliver.
cx: Wondering whether to stop before 34 weeks.

q: My husband is supportive of me stopping at 34 weeks like we planned but I don’t think I can make it that far and I don’t know how to tell him because I’m so embarrassed about it.
cx: The leave plan they made together.

q: I just feel like I’m having to get all my own information off the internet and Reddit and stuff, which I guess is fine, but I would love to get a bit from my own doctors.
cx: Same author as the work post; 24 weeks, rushed appointments, results never explained.

q: They’ve never even mentioned like what hospital they deliver at
cx: After three OB appointments.

q: Then she was like “Okay you guys are good now.” again, and I was to nervous to ask anything else since I knew the office was closing soon
cx: Her midwife ended the visit before she asked about work restrictions.

q: Firstly, they had my due date wrong by almost 2.5 weeks.
cx: The office used her period date, not her early scan.

q: So this is just sounding like a red flag to me of the office wanting to get another scan, which is not accurate for size anyway, so they can lead me down the road to induction or C-section due to size.
cx: At 34 weeks, offered a 37-week growth scan after a borderline screening result; she declined.

q: So all that stress was for nothing and they kept telling me the wrong answer over messages.
cx: The office said no water before a test; the lab tech said water was fine.

q: People say oh it goes by so fast. Not true for me. I’m not even halfway and it’s has felt like eternity.
cx: At 19 weeks, still nauseous and sleepless, struggling to work.

q: I need to go to work and I just don’t have the energy to. I never expected this level of tiredness.
cx: After weeks at home sick.

q: It’s confusing when I get different opinions.
cx: 5.5 weeks postpartum, two doctors disagreeing about her recovery.

q: It’s been really hard to accept how much resting is required and I have horrible mom guilt for not showing up as much for my toddler or helping my fiance around the house.
cx: Slow recovery with a toddler at home.

q: I’ve been overwhelmed with social media and all the things advertised over there.
cx: First-time mother, UK-born, living in the Middle East.

q: Where I live I only get 6 weeks maternity leave including weekends 😭😭 I want to take a year too if it’s possible.
cx: Comparing leave with a woman elsewhere.

q: I started the job when I found out I was pregnant and it’s a startup. No such thing as maternity cover jobs here either!
cx: Plans to tell her remote employer in June or July.

q: I live in a very hot country so I think the heat is affecting me too.
cx: Her list of first-trimester milestones.

q: My partner sees this difference and wonders: how can you be so tired if you worked full time with our first?
cx: 27 weeks with her second, working three days a week.

q: I feel like I’m being judged by my family as sleeping too much/ lazy/ making excuses.
cx: Sleeping 9–10 hours plus naps.

q: I seem to be giving more responsibility of my daughter eg making her dinner and putting her to bed onto my partner because by 5pm I am like a zombie.
cx: How the older child's care has shifted.
